Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + rationale

Hi Jenna —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the model shortlist we discussed based on Acme's constraints (batching for high throughput, 300 token average request, and strict 50ms p95 latency target for Tier 1 traffic):

What we heard
- Primary workload: real-time summarization + intent extraction for support chat (300 tokens avg).
- Volume: ~250k reqs/day currently, spike to 500k on peak days.
- SLO: p95 latency <= 50ms for interactive path; cost target ~ $0.0008/req (target).
- Quality: high priority for preserving factuality in summaries; some tolerance for light hallucination only if we can validate via post-processing.

Recommended model shortlist (tradeoffs summary) — attached playbook with detail: acme_model_shortlist_playbook.pdf
1) redwood-7b-q4 (recommended primary) — Best balance: high quality for summarization, modest latency (25-40ms p95 on our Dedicated m60-like nodes with continuous batching), and moderate cost. Good for rollout as default.
2) redwood-3b-int8 (lower-cost fallback) — Lower cost and lower latency (15-25ms p95) for high-throughput routes; slight drop in abstractive quality on edge cases. Great for bulk/cheap path.
3) open-llama-13b-4bit (quality-first option) — Highest raw quality on long-form summarization tests but higher cost and latency (50-80ms p95); recommend for non-interactive batch jobs or canary top-tier users.
4) safety-filter-embed (embedding + rerank) — Use as a pre-filter to improve factuality and reduce downstream hallucination risk (very low cost).

Key evals we ran (links in the attached CSV + HTML): acme_benchmark_results_10-22.csv and https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/benchmarks/acme-2026-10-22.html
- Head-to-head on Acme prompt set (attached prompt_set_acme_v1.jsonl)
- Latency and cost matrix per model (redwood_cost_latency_matrix.xlsx)

Quality regression concerns
- We observed a 6% regression on entity preservation for redwood-3b-int8 vs redwood-7b-q4 on the eval set; recommend adding a lightweight post-process reranking step (safety-filter-embed) and monitoring set-level metrics in Redwood Console.

Proposed next steps
- Monica (CS) to run an in-production A/B pilot for 2 weeks comparing redwood-7b-q4 vs redwood-3b-int8 on a 10% traffic split (metrics: p95 latency, cost/req, summary fidelity).
- Jenna/Acme: review shortlist and confirm which model(s) you want in the pilot.
- I'll share our cost/commit pilot proposal if you want reserved capacity (Dedicated) for predictable p95 and lower unit cost.

Available times to sync next week: Tue/Wed 11-2 PT.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Jenna —

Great questions. Short answers first, details below.

1) redwood-7b-q4 latency context: the numbers I quoted are for a warm KV cache with continuous batching enabled on Dedicated m60-like instances in us-west. With a cold cache (first-time prefixes) you can expect an additional ~10-20ms p95 hit. Given your traffic profile (many repeated prefixes) warm numbers are realistic for the pilot.

2) 6% entity-preservation regression on redwood-3b-int8: failure modes we saw are primarily truncation/abstraction where the model condenses or omits secondary entities (phone numbers, minor product IDs) rather than inventing new entities. Hallucinations were rare (<1% of examples) but present; reranking with the embedding filter recovers ~70% of the dropped entities in our tests. Full failure-mode notes are in acme_benchmark_results_10-22.csv.

3) safety-filter-embed added latency: in our baseline setup it added ~8-12ms on top of model latency for a vector lookup + simple rerank. If you colocate the embedder and use async prefiltering, you can largely hide that cost in the pipeline.

Files shared: prompt_set_acme_v1.jsonl (sample prompts + expected outputs), acme_benchmark_results_10-22.csv (detailed failure modes), redwood_cost_latency_matrix.xlsx (cost numbers). I put the public benchmark HTML here: https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/benchmarks/acme-2026-10-22.html.

Monica — can your team take Jenna's eval suite share and spin up the pilot configuration? Proposed traffic split: 90% redwood-7b-q4, 10% redwood-3b-int8 for 2 weeks, with a canary date to flip 50/50 if initial metrics look good.

Jenna — Tue 11:30 PT works. I'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Thanks,
Marissa
